title: Scalarization intertwines inverse representation transport and weight minus n slash
statement: Let n∈ℕ, E:ℍ→BinaryForm ℂ n, σ∈SL₂(ℤ), and τ∈ℍ. Put p(z)=E(z)(1,−z) and G(z)=binaryFormRepSL ℂ n (σ⁻¹)(E(σz)). Then (p|_{−n}σ)(τ)=G(τ)(1,−τ). No differentiability or equivariance hypothesis is needed.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : UpperHalfPlane → ↥(HeckeEis.BinaryForm ℂ n)) (σ : Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℤ) (τ : UpperHalfPlane), (SlashAction.map (-(n : ℤ)) σ (fun z : UpperHalfPlane => MvPolynomial.eval (fun j : Fin 2 => if j = 0 then 1 else -(z : ℂ)) (E z).val)) τ = MvPolynomial.eval (fun j : Fin 2 => if j = 0 then 1 else -(τ : ℂ)) (((HeckeEis.binaryFormRepSL ℂ n) σ⁻¹) (E (σ • τ))).val
